messages:
alex: Heads up — after the node image push to `cuda-driver:535` + `nccl 2.20.x` we started seeing a steady build-up of pending inference requests in ap-southeast-1. Queue depth spiked ~08:12 UTC and stayed high.
kim: repro? single model or fleet-wide?
maria: fleet-wide for multi-GPU inference only. Single-GPU jobs look fine. Symptoms are collective calls stalling during KV cache sync stage.
alex: here's a short snippet from the worker logs around the hang (trimmed):
```
[2026-03-17T08:12:45Z] kvsync: starting collective(ALL) seq=12546
[2026-03-17T08:12:46Z] nccl: op allreduce id=0x7fae... waiting for peers
[2026-03-17T08:12:47Z] nccl: timeout after 30s, aborting
[2026-03-17T08:13:15Z] inference: request timed out, retrying
```
devon: We saw identical stack traces from two different AZs in the region, both on A100s. No obvious driver OOM. nvidia-smi looks normal, but processes stuck in `ncclCommInitRank`.
kim: did the image bump include any kernel or NIC firmware updates? RDMA stack change could explain collective stalls.
maria: node image diff: driver 525 -> 535, cuda 11.8 -> 12.1, nccl 2.18.4 -> 2.20.3, ipxe/firmware unchanged. No NIC firmware change. We also rolled kubelet 1.28 for those nodes.
alex: quick mitigation: we set NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 on a canary pool and latency/backpressure disappeared for those pods. That suggests IB/RDMA/UCX interaction with the new nccl build.
ops-jen: good find. Can we bake that env var into the autoscaler for ap-southeast while we investigate? It has cost impact (falls back to TCP-ish path) but avoids timeouts.
devon: created a canary config and routed 10% of traffic to pooled nodes with NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 — success for the last 30m. Will scale to 50% if stable.
kim: dbs: we need a repro harness that accelerates the problem. Maria, can you run the nccL microbench in a tight loop across 8x A100 on a drained node image with 2.20 and record `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO`? capture `dmesg` too.
maria: running now. early logs show repeated ``NCCL WARN Call to ibv_post_send failed errno=11`` on some ranks.
alex: that errno smells like EAGAIN on verbs. Could be queue pair exhaustion or incompatibility with kernel verbs ABI.
devon: FYI we also tested with NCCL_SOCKET_IFNAME set to `eth0` and it didn't help — only disabling IB avoided the stall.
kim: for quick rollback options: 1) pin workloads to older node image with nccl 2.18, 2) keep IB disabled (NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1), 3) roll back driver/cuda if we can reproduce driver-specific bug.
ops-jen: org ask: what is expected SLA impact if we pin to old image? We lose capacity for planned upgrades; some pods need newer CUDA for new models.
alex: pinning will reduce available upgraded pool by ~30% for the next 48h — customers on private/dedicated may see slower provisioning. Cost wise ~+12% on spot usage due to constrained pool.
maria: I opened a ticket with NVIDIA (case #R-INF-7621) attaching traces and `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` logs. Also pushed reproducer to ci-infra: `tests/nccl/collective_hang_repro`.
kim: good. meanwhile create an alert for sudden rise in `nccl_wait_time` and backpressure across routes — we missed the first 10 minutes because the metric only rolled up every 15m.
devon: PR to autoscaler: add a temporary label `nccl-ib-disabled=true` which forces that env into node groups. Canary deploy in progress.
ops-jen: are there other regions with the same node image rollout? we should avoid repeating.
alex: rollout schedule: us-east-1 next on Monday. Pause that and run the repro + vendor contact first.
maria: summary of mitigations and next steps in one line: 1) canary env NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1 applied and scaled to 50%; 2) block further node image rollouts; 3) NVIDIA engaged with logs+traces; 4) prepare rollback image pinned to nccl 2.18.
devon: adding runbook note: if collective hangs spike, set `NCCL_IB_DISABLE=1` and roll traffic to canary node pool; do not reboot nodes unless asked by NVIDIA.
kim: also document that enabling `NCCL_DEBUG=INFO` can be verbose. use it only on repro nodes. Toggle `NCCL_ASYNC_ERROR_HANDLING=1` for slightly better recovery during testing.
alex: thanks everyone — I'll follow up once NVIDIA responds and after we have a kernel/driver hypothesis. For now ap-southeast capacity is ~70% and stable on canary.
deploy-bot: [build] ci-infra:tests/nccl/collective_hang_repro passed on nccl-2.18 image.
maria: note for postmortem: this looked like an RDMA/verbs regression exposed by nccl 2.20 driver combo. We'll capture timeline once root cause confirmed.
